title: Carbon — curated atomic gas supplement and existing table inventory, 2026-10-06
body:
# Carbon — curated atomic gas supplement and existing table inventory, 2026-10-06

Stage: IMPLEMENTED. Actual terminal verification is recorded in the [batch receipt](../../data/quality/thermal-carbon-batch-2026-10-06.json). Full scientific and image acceptance remains PARTIAL.

## Preserved owners and inventory

The [unchanged master](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/data/structured/0006-Carbon-C.yaml) owns neutral MAT:0006:ATOM:C at /states/0. Diamond, graphite, graphene, nanotube, fullerene, amorphous and compound owners retain separate contexts. Ten authored tables had permanent filename IDs 001–010 but no manifest. The new [table inventory](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/data/structured/0006-Carbon-C-Table-Manifest.yaml) links their actual titles, IDs, files and hashes without editing them or accepting their science. Their content review remains pending. Thermal table 011 and graph 013 are additive; all twelve existing [graph reservations](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/data/structured/0006-Carbon-C-Graph-Manifest.yaml) remain intact, including ungenerated graph 012. The authored parent and graph-manifest prefixes are byte-identical.

## Primary source and applicability

The [NIST gas page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440440&Units=SI&Mask=1) identifies C, CAS 7440-44-0, InChI=1S/C. Its Chase (1998) GAS fit covers **298–6000 K**, on **mol C** basis, with March 1983 review comment. [Exact coefficient bytes](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0006-2026-10-06.html.txt) and [publisher table bytes](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0006-2026-10-06-table.html.txt) retain SHA-256 provenance. All **59 publisher rows / 177 Cp-S-H comparisons** agree at printed precision; no boundary rounding resolution was needed. All 101 accepted samples have finite functions and positive heat capacity; derivative checks passed. New **SRC-000513** has no equivalent Carbon WebBook work in the [existing registry](../../data/registries/sources.yaml); **SRC-000085 CODATA** remains a distinct original work.

This interval includes 298.15 K, so evaluation there is allowed. The value describes the specified atomic gas standard-state species and does not establish stable ambient gas, equilibrium abundance, or diamond/graphite heat capacity. Retain the published enthalpy offset without forcing a reference-temperature residual to zero. Alias links and shared elemental formula are insufficient to equate species or material states. The [condensed page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440440&Units=SI&Mask=2) was inspected as a private diagnostic; none of its observations or functions is imported. Applied pressure, isotope fractions and coefficient uncertainty/covariance remain UNKNOWN. No C/C2/C3 equilibrium, ionisation fraction, latent heat, phase boundary or arbitrary-pressure EOS is inferred.

## Outputs and verification boundary

The [reader chapter](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/0006-Carbon-C-Thermochemistry.md), [structured evaluation](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/data/structured/0006-Carbon-C-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml), [readable table](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/tables/0006-Carbon-C-TABLE-011-Thermodynamic-Functions.md), [CSV](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/tables/0006-Carbon-C-TABLE-011-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) and [SVG](../../records/0006-Carbon-C/graphs/0006-Carbon-C-GRAPH-013-Heat-Capacity.svg) use the same source, neutral owner, units, interval and unknowns. Existing curated subject, slot and append contracts and the native plot generator are reused; no production-code or schema change. Root actually inspected the native PNG. The supplemental chart earns zero standalone-image credit.

Source transcription, publisher comparisons, Python/JavaScript arithmetic, artifact checks and root visual inspection are recorded separately. Both auxiliary review workers returned an account usage-limit error; no independent reviewer PASS is claimed. Independent scientific review and experimental replication remain pending. Software test/build/browser/copy results are recorded only after terminal completion in the receipt.

Global coverage: 41 thermal owners / 140 fits / 14,140 calculated rows /71 bounded thermal gaps /269 supplemental charts. All 119 canonical records remain represented; all 143 master tasks, 4248 confirmed-domain reviews and 2587 standalone confirmed-element panels remain pending. The [existing selector](../../data/research/mat-update-review.json), [MAT TODO](../../data/quality/MAT-TODO.json) and [handoff](../../MAT_CODEX_CONTINUATION_HANDOFF.md) retain these boundaries.

## Next executable requirement

Audit Nitrogen 0007 and primary sources for its declared molecular N2 GAS state. MAT:0007:MOL:N2 is at /ordinary_molecular_state; keep neutral atomic MAT:0007:ATOM:N at /states/0 and molecular, isotope, magnetic, reactive-nitrogen and condensed owners separate. A mol N2 fit describes one mole of N2 molecules containing two moles of N atoms; do not relabel it as mol N or infer spin-isomer/equilibrium fractions. 10 physical tables reserve IDs 001–010; no table manifest exists, so inventory their existing IDs/files additively before adding another table. 12 graph reservations occupy 001–012; reviewed candidates are table 011/graph 013 subject to fresh physical/manifest collision checks. SRC-000102 already owns the Nitrogen WebBook work; preserve its spectroscopy metadata and use same_work_as for an accepted dated retrieval of the same work. Recompute the next unreserved source ID; repeat primary source, formula/state, units, range, publisher and work-dedup checks before acceptance. Continue 0008–0012 individually afterwards. Universal atomic-child projection, 71 bounded thermal source gaps, transport/dynamics/multiphysics/domain acceptance, historical source metadata/documentation, independent Carbon review and remaining standalone images remain pending; MAT stays PARTIAL.

sources.scope_note: No equivalent Carbon WebBook work found in the existing registry. SRC-000085 CODATA remains a distinct original work with unchanged metadata. Auxiliary independent reviewer unavailable due to account usage limit.
sources.scope: The exact GAS fit species is C with InChI=1S/C: neutral monatomic carbon, not C2, C3, carbon ions or an equilibrium vapor mixture. One mole of source species is one mole of C atoms. Shared CAS/formula aliases and links to diamond/graphite do not make this gas fit a condensed-material function. One GAS fit covers 298–6000 K. The separately retained condensed page is a private diagnostic; none of its observations or fits is accepted or bound to the neutral atomic GAS owner. No evaluation below 298 K is justified. The valid fit does permit evaluation at 298.15 K, but gas functions at low temperatures describe the specified standard-state species, not the stable ambient solid or equilibrium gas abundance. Source limits do not establish a gas stability or phase boundary. Existing C-12/C-13/C-14 records, atomic-weight and metrological references retain separate scope. No isotope-specific functions or isotope fractions follow from the fit or listed molecular weight. The Shomate equations have no pressure variable. Applied pressure, arbitrary-pressure EOS and phase diagrams are not inferred; original one-bar standard-entropy rows have their own reference context. No C/C2/C3 equilibrium fraction, molecular dissociation, ionisation fraction, charge-state mixture or nuclear-spin population is calculated. Published enthalpy reference offsets are retained. No gas-to-diamond/graphite transition path, latent heat or equilibrium phase diagram is constructed. Coefficient uncertainty and covariance are unreported. Source output rounding and derivative residuals are software/source-format checks, not physical uncertainty. Separate CODATA review uncertainties are not coefficient errors. Direct source transcription and independent Python/JavaScript arithmetic checks do not establish independent calorimetry, experimental replication or complete Carbon thermophysics. Auxiliary human/model-independent review is unavailable due to the account usage limit.
